idea: Mid-twenties South London lad with an Estuary accent: clipped, clinical urgency that cracks into raw disbelief. This is the most 'Casualty' option and sounds furthest from a posh minister.
script:
Sats dropping — he's peri-arrest!

...Why have we stopped?!
tone: A young English man in his mid twenties with a thick South London accent, working class and everyday, an NHS paramedic in the back of an ambulance at night. The first line is fast, low and clipped, breathless, focused on the patient, professional under pressure. The second line bursts out louder and higher, genuinely bewildered and angry, his voice cracking. Natural and real like a British television hospital drama, close to the microphone, dry voice only.
